requirement: Implement a ConcurrencyLimiter worker pool using asyncio.Semaphore to bound concurrent jobs to max_concurrency (>0), tracking active/peak concurrency and completed/failed jobs, ensuring semaphore tokens are released cleanly on job exceptions, and providing an async run_batch entrypoint using asyncio.TaskGroup.
skeleton: Asyncio concurrency controller managing worker pool throughput with atomic telemetry.
caption: A pure-asyncio module with two definitions and no third-party dependency. LimiterStats is a frozen dataclass with five integer fields: max_concurrency, peak_concurrency, active_count, completed_count, and failed_count. ConcurrencyLimiter takes max_concurrency with a default of 4 and raises ValueError when the value is zero or negative; on success it stores the limit, creates an asyncio.Semaphore of that size, an asyncio.Lock guarding the counters, and zeroed active, peak, completed, and failed counters. The execute coroutine takes a zero-argument callable returning an awaitable, acquires the semaphore with async with, increments active under the lock and raises peak when active exceeds it, then awaits the job inside a try block: a normal result increments completed and is returned, an Exception increments failed and is re-raised, and the finally clause decrements active under the lock, so the semaphore slot is always returned when the async with block exits, whether or not the job failed. run_batch opens an asyncio.TaskGroup, creates one task per job through execute, and after the group closes collects each task's result into a list in submission order. get_stats returns a LimiterStats snapshot of the limit and all four counters, and reset_state rebuilds the semaphore at the configured size and zeroes every counter. The type variable T threads the job's return type through execute and run_batch.

rationale.teaches: A bounded worker pool: a Semaphore sized by max_concurrency, tokens released even when a job raises, honest active/peak/completed/failed counters, and a TaskGroup batch entry point.
rationale.why: A concurrency limit is invisible in any single run. The observable is peak concurrency under load and whether capacity survives failures, which a fixture can measure with a counter inside the jobs.

candidates.why_wrong: The semaphore token is not released when a job raises, so each failure permanently removes one slot until the pool starves.
max_concurrency=0 is accepted and builds a zero-capacity semaphore, so run_batch blocks forever.
A Lock replaces the Semaphore, so at most one job runs at a time whatever max_concurrency says.
A failed job increments the completed counter, so telemetry reports failures as successes.
The default pool size is 1 instead of 4, so callers relying on the documented default get serialized execution.
